title: Three questions decide every cached response
purpose: Connect the cache key, the freshness check and revalidation into one decision for HTML pages and hashed assets.
sequence_reason: The cache asks its questions in a fixed order, and each answer decides the next question, so a short sequence fits.
summary: A cache answers three questions in order: is there a stored copy for this key, is it fresh, and if not, does the origin answer 304 or 200. The directives set the answers: no-store, no-cache, max-age and s-maxage. A common pattern gives HTML no-cache with an ETag and hashed assets a one-year max-age with immutable.
explanation: The key, the lifetime and the validator together decide hit, revalidate or miss for every request.

learning_check.question: Which header set fits an HTML page that must never show an old version but should stay cheap to check?
learning_check.answer: Cache-Control: no-cache with an ETag, so every reuse is a small conditional request that usually ends in 304.

scenes.heading: Three questions, every request
scenes.narration: Three questions decide every cached response. The cache asks them in the same order each time.

scenes.heading: The cache asks in this order
scenes.narration: First, is there a stored copy for this key? Second, is it fresh? Third, if stale, does the origin answer 304 or 200?

items: Stored copy for this key? Key: URL plus Vary headers

scenes.heading: Directives set the answers
scenes.narration: no-store means never store. no-cache means store, but check first. max-age gives seconds of freshness, and s-maxage does so for shared caches.

scenes.heading: HTML page versus hashed asset
scenes.narration: Give the HTML page no-cache and an ETag, so it is never stale. Give hashed assets a one-year max-age and immutable.

visual.verdict: Pages stay current; assets never wait
